# Servo 0.1: Embeddable Engine on crates.io

## Thesis

On **2026-04-13** the Servo project published **`servo` 0.1.0** on [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/servo) — the first release of the engine **as a library**, not only as the `servoshell` demo browser. The `0.1` version number is deliberate: the team has not defined what **1.0** means yet, but the bump signals growing confidence that the **embedding API** is usable for real embedders. Monthly crates keep moving (by late 2026 the crate line includes **0.7.x** regular releases plus a parallel **0.1.x LTS** line). This chapter teaches the mental model of embedding Servo: what the crate is for, what `0.1` vs LTS vs monthly means, and which build/feature knobs matter — without downloading the engine’s enormous dependency graph in the book lab.

Toolchain note: examples assume a recent stable Rust. This authoring host has **rustc 1.99.0**. Current `servo` releases advertise **MSRV 1.88.0** (see crates.io); LTS migration notes may raise clang and Rust floors when you jump major LTS lines.

## Mental model

```text
  Your application (windowing, input, IPC, privileges)
           │
           │  embedding API (servo crate + embedder traits)
           ▼
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Servo library                                        │
  │  constellation · script · layout · paint · net · …    │
  │  optional: webgl / webgpu / webxr / media-gstreamer   │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
           │
           ▼
  OS graphics / audio / network backends (surfman, etc.)
```

| Concept | Meaning |
|---------|---------|
| **`servo` crate** | The embeddable engine on crates.io (MPL-2.0) |
| **`servoshell`** | Demo browser — **not** published to crates.io; build from the GitHub tree |
| **0.1.0 milestone** | First library release; embedding API “good enough for some users,” not a stability covenant |
| **Monthly / regular line** | Fast-moving; breaking changes expected between minors |
| **LTS line** | Best-effort ~6-month cadence, ~9-month support, **security fixes only**; may need `git` deps for CVE backports |
| **`servo-embedder-traits`** | Hooks embedders implement (e.g. custom resource readers) |
| **`baked-in-resources` / `bundled`** | Default path that embeds default resources in the binary; disable and supply your own reader if you need that |

**Risk profile (from the Servo book):** rendering **known, trusted** content inside your app is a different threat model from a general-purpose browser that loads the open web. Evaluate accordingly — Servo is still pre-1.0.

## Worked examples

### Case 1: Read the milestone announcement, then pin deliberately

The [0.1.0 blog post](https://servo.org/blog/2026/04/13/servo-0.1.0-release/) is the historical milestone. For new work in late 2026 you typically choose:

| Goal | Pinning strategy |
|------|------------------|
| Track features / file upstream bugs easily | Latest regular release on crates.io (e.g. `0.7.x`) |
| Ship a product with scheduled upgrades | Current **LTS** (see [LTS release](https://book.servo.org/embedding/lts-release.html) in the Servo book) |
| Reproduce a 0.1-era tutorial | `servo = "=0.1.0"` (expect migration work later) |

```toml
# Cargo.toml — illustrative pins (check crates.io before locking)
[dependencies]
# Regular line (example version as of 2026-10; bump intentionally):
servo = "0.7"

# Or an LTS / milestone pin when you need a slower moving API:
# servo = "=0.1.4"
```

Do **not** treat `0.1` as “more stable than 0.7” merely because the number is smaller — on crates.io, `0.1.x` after the LTS decision is the **long-term** branch family, while `0.2`–`0.7` are the regular train. Read the Servo book’s LTS page before you pick.

### Case 2: Embedding API shape (no full build in this chapter)

Documentation for embedding lives under [The Servo Book → Embedding](https://book.servo.org/embedding/overview.html). The stable ideas:

1. Depend on the **`servo`** library crate (not servoshell).
2. Drive the engine from your event loop: create a `Servo` / builder, feed input, composite frames into your windowing stack.
3. Decide **resources**: keep default `bundled` / `baked-in-resources`, or disable default features and call `servo_embedder_traits::submit_resource_reader` with your own `ResourceReader` (OpenHarmony’s filesystem reader is the cited pattern upstream).
4. Select **feature flags** deliberately. Modularization moved many web features behind flags; LTS migration notes recommend considering `default_web_features` when you want the broad web surface.

```rust
// embed_sketch.rs — API orientation only (will not compile without the servo crate
// and platform deps). Do not cargo-add servo in the book lab: the dependency
// tree and system libraries (e.g. gstreamer for media) are large.
//
// use servo::ServoBuilder; // names evolve — follow the book for your pin
//
// fn main() {
//     let mut servo = ServoBuilder::new(/* embedder handles */)
//         // .prefs(...)
//         .build();
//     // pump events → servo.handle_events(...) → present frames
// }
fn main() {
    println!("See https://book.servo.org/embedding/overview.html for current builders");
}
```

```console
$ rustc --version
rustc 1.99.0 (b940084d7 2026-09-28)
$ rustc embed_sketch.rs -o /tmp/embed_sketch && /tmp/embed_sketch
See https://book.servo.org/embedding/overview.html for current builders
```

### Case 3: Building without `./mach` (embedder perspective)

Upstream notes that embedding builds often go through **`cargo`** directly, but `./mach` normally sets environment variables and enables **`media-gstreamer`** by default. If you bypass mach:

- Run `./mach print-env` on a Servo checkout when cross-compiling (Android / OpenHarmony) and mirror those variables.
- Expect to install platform media/graphics dependencies yourself if you enable gstreamer features.
- Prefer feature flags over “copy servoshell’s Cargo.toml blindly.”

This book chapter **does not** run `cargo add servo` or `./mach bootstrap` — both pull toolchains and system packages beyond the no-install lab policy. Use the Servo book’s “Building servo without mach” section on a dedicated machine.

### Case 4: Migrating off 0.1 LTS (preview)

The Servo book’s “Migrating from 0.1 to 0.6 LTS” list is the boring checklist when you finally jump:

- Enable **`default_web_features`** (or an explicit subset) after modularization.
- Re-validate **prefs** — unknown preference names can **panic**.
- Update mouse button enums (`Left/Middle/Right` → `Primary/Auxiliary/Secondary`).
- Relocate WebXR registry registration as documented for your target version.
- Budget for **MSRV** and **clang** bumps on the new LTS.

Read the full list for your target LTS; do not crochet a partial migrate.

## The trap

1. **Publishing or depending on servoshell.** The demo browser is not the embeddable product line on crates.io.
2. **Assuming crates.io LTS patches always exist.** Security backports may force **`git` dependencies** when MSRV blocks a crates.io bump — plan for that in corporate allow-lists.
3. **Leaving default features on “for convenience” on constrained devices.** Media, WebGL, WebGPU, and WebXR are heavy; turn on what you need.
4. **Treating 0.1 as production-complete.** The project is explicit: no 1.0 definition yet. Trusted-content widgets ≠ full browser replacement.
5. **Skipping resource ownership.** If you disable baked-in resources and forget a `ResourceReader`, startup fails in confusing ways. The OpenHarmony example is the reference pattern.

## The boring rule

Depend on the **`servo` library crate**, pick **regular vs LTS** on purpose, keep **servoshell** out of your `Cargo.toml`, and follow [book.servo.org/embedding](https://book.servo.org/embedding/overview.html) for the builder/event-loop API on the version you pinned. Evaluate threat model before you point the engine at untrusted URLs.

## Try this

1. Open [crates.io/crates/servo](https://crates.io/crates/servo) and list the latest regular version vs the latest `0.1.x`. Write one sentence on which you would pin for a shipping app and why.
2. Read the embedding overview and LTS pages in the Servo book; sketch your app’s event-loop ownership on paper (who owns the window, who calls into Servo).
3. On a disposable machine (not this no-install lab), create a hello-embed crate against an LTS pin and run *only* what the book’s embedding chapter shows — then stop before enabling every feature flag.
4. Skim the 0.1→0.6 migration notes and mark which items would touch your sketch.
